problems.title: Nitrate in groundwater
problems.problem:
Problem 2 (16 points). Nitrate in groundwater

[Open questions, total 36 points.]

Nitrates are substances that are found in animal excretions. When over-fertilization occurs, the nitrates can end up in groundwater. This will eventually have a negative impact on the quality of the drinking water that is prepared from groundwater. In a number of places the acceptable concentration of 50 mg nitrates per liter of groundwater is already exceeded.

In order to determine how much nitrate is present in groundwater, all of the nitrate must first be converted to ammonia. This is done with aluminium in an alkaline environment, where the aluminium is converted into aluminate, $\ce{AlO2-}$.

1 (5 points) Provide the equations of both half reactions involved in this conversion and then deduce the final equation of the reaction. $\ce{OH-}$ and $\ce{H2O}$ are present in both half reactions.

The reaction between aluminium and nitrate is carried out in a distillation flask. By boiling the liquid, all of the ammonia that is produced, is collected in a flask containing a hydrochloric acid solution.
The above-mentioned investigation is conducted using 3.00 liter of groundwater. All of the ammonia is collected in a flask that contains 35.0 ml of 0.202 M hydrochloric acid solution. The contents of the flask is then titrated with caustic soda. This titration is conducted in such a manner that the excess hydrochloric acid is neutralized, but only a very small amount of the ammonium has reacted.

To achieve this, methyl red is used as indicator and the titration is completed when the pH = 6.2.

2 (3 points) Indicate, using a calculation that, at pH = 6.2, only a very small amount of the ammonium has reacted.

The titration required 26.5 mL of 0.195 M caustic soda.

3 (4 points) Use a calculation to determine whether the groundwater meets the above-mentioned quality standard

If the above-mentioned method is applied to groundwater that contains not only nitrates, but also ammonium, an inaccurate nitrate content will be found.
In this case, the above-mentioned method can be adapted in order to determine the nitrate and ammonium content separately.

4 (4 points) Give a general description of how the above-mentioned method can be adapted and indicate how both the nitrate and ammonium content can be determined. Note: no calculations are necessary.

problems.title: Bisphenol A
problems.problem:
Problem 3 (20 points). Bisphenol A

Bisphenol is the collective name for a large number of compounds, of which the molecules contain two phenol groups. The most well-known bisphenol is bisphenol A, usually abbreviated with BPA:

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/nl-2022-1-11-fig1.png

BPA is prepared by allowing phenol (benzenol) and acetone (propanone) to react with each other. Besides BPA, one other substance is produced during the reaction

5 (4 points) Provide the reaction equation for the formation of BPA. Use structural formulas for the organic compounds.

Another bisphenol is bisphenol Z, BPZ:

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/nl-2022-1-11-fig2.png

6 (2 points) Provide the structural formula of the compound that is needed to react with phenol to produce BPZ.

BPA is used as the starting material for the production of certain polymers. Below is the structural formula of a section from the middle of a molecule of one of these polymers.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/nl-2022-1-11-fig3.png

Polymers can be identified in different ways. We distinguish copolymers and non-copolymers, and also thermoplastics and thermosets.

7 (4 points) To which of the abovementioned type(s) of polymers does the abovementioned polymer belong? Provide an explanation for your answers.

Polymers of BPA are often used in packaging of food. When this sort of packaging is heated, for example the sterilizing of baby bottles or heating of ready-to-eat meals in the microwave, BPA can be released through the hydrolysis of the ester bonds in the polymer. It can also happen during contact with alkaline food products or cleaning agents.

8 (2 points) Provide the formula of the particles, other than BPA molecules, that are also produced by the complete hydrolysis of the above-mentioned polymer in an alkaline environment.

Due to the large scale on which BPA is used, almost everyone in the Western world has BPA in their bodies. BPA is classified as an irritant and is toxic, which is why it can have negative consequences on one’s health.

BPA is also present in surface water as well as in drinking water. BPA is able to dissolve in dichloromethane better than it does in water, which is a characteristic used when the BPA content of drinking water needs to be determined. Also BPA-d16 is used as a reference substance. In molecules of BPA-d16 all sixteen hydrogen atoms have mass number 2. Such hydrogen atoms are called deuterium atoms. The following method can be used in such a determination.
1. An extra amount of $5.0\,\mathrm{\mu L}$ (microliter) of a solution containing $1.0\,\mathrm{\mu g}$ BPA per mL, is added to 500 mL drinking water, that contains BPA.
2. 15 g $\ce{NaCl}$ is then dissolved in the above solution, after which the pH is adjusted to 4.0 by adding phosphoric acid.
3. The acidic solution is then extracted with 30 mL of dichloromethane, after which the dichloromethane layer is separated from the water layer.
4. This extraction is repeated twice.
5. Subsequently the three dichloromethane fractions are combined and then evaporated to a volume of roughly 5 mL.
6. $7.0\,\mathrm{\mu L}$ of a reference substance, containing $1.0\,\mathrm{\mu g}$ BPA-d16 per mL, is added to the remaining solution.
7. A small sample of the solution which then is formed, is injected into a gas chromatograph. After obtaining the chromatogram (chromatogram 1), the peak areas of BPA and BPA-d16 are determined.
8. Steps 1 to 7 is also conducted with pure water. Another chromatogram (chromatogram 2) is obtained, where the peak areas of BPA and BPA-d16 are determined.

During an investigation of drinking water, the following values were obtained (the areas are given in arbitrary units):

$$\begin{array}{l|l|l} & \text{peak area of BPA} & \text{peak area of BPA-d16} \\ \hline \text{chromatogram 1 (drinking water)} & 235 & 5987 \\ \hline \text{chromatogram 2 (pure water)} & 25 & 1873 \end{array}$$

9 Calculate the BPA content in the sample of drinking water in $\mathrm{ng\,L^{-1}}$. Assume that all BPA present in the original sample is present in the dichloromethane.

Some students discuss this determination of BPA. Joris finds that steps 5 and 7 are inaccurate. He thinks that the results will be more accurate if the volume of dichloromethane in step 5 is brought to precisely 5.00 mL and that in step 7 the ‘small sample’ of the solution that is injected into the chromatograph should be more precisely specified, for example $20\,\mathrm{\mu L}$. Jorinde says that no BPA-d16 is necessary when the determination is carried out according to Joris’s suggestions.

10 (2 points) Does it have an effect on the accuracy of the final result when the experiment is carried out according to Joris’s suggestions? And is it also true that in that case no BPA-d16 needs to be used? Copy the following sentences and make the correct choices for the italic printed words therein.
• The result of the determination becomes more accurate / is equally accurate / becomes more inaccurate.
• BPA-d16 is / is not needed when the determination is carried out according to Joris’s suggestions.

problems.problem:
Problem 2 (19 points). Gold in solution

[Open questions, total 37 points.]

Gold is a noble metal; there are almost no acids that will react with it. One of the few liquids that gold will react with is aqua regia. Aqua regia is a mixture of concentrated hydrochloric acid and concentrated nitric acid in a volume ratio of 3.0 : 1.0. The molarity of concentrated hydrochloric acid is $12\,\mathrm{mol\,L^{-1}}$ and the molarity of concentrated nitric acid is $15\,\mathrm{mol\,L^{-1}}$.

Aqua regia has a very low pH.

1 (3 points) Calculate the pH of aqua regia. Provide your answer in the correct number of significant figures. Assume that both acids are fully ionised.

When gold reacts with aqua regia, the gold is mainly converted into $\ce{AuCl4-}$ ions. Nitrogen dioxide is also produced. This is a redox reaction.

2 (3 points) Provide the equations of both half-reactions for this redox reaction and the complete reaction equation.

When you only account for the $V^0$ values of these half-reactions, which are listed in Binas or ScienceData, you could conclude that this redox reaction cannot take place.

3 (1 point) Provide a possible explanation for why this redox reaction takes place anyway.

Besides $\ce{AuCl4-}$ ions, there are also $\ce{AuCl2-}$ ions. However, $\ce{AuCl2-}$ ions are instable; at room temperature they are converted into solid gold and $\ce{AuCl4-}$. This is an equilibrium reaction. The incomplete reaction equation for this conversion is:

$$\ce{AuCl2^-(aq) <=> Au(s) + AuCl4^-(aq) + Cl^-(aq)} \qquad \text{equilibrium I}$$

The only thing missing from this equation are the coefficients.

4 (3 points) Copy the equation above to your answer sheet and complete it.

In order to determine the equilibrium constant for equilibrium I, a mixture is investigated in which equilibrium I has been established. In this equilibrium mixture, the only negative ions present are $\ce{AuCl4-}$, $\ce{AuCl2-}$ and $\ce{Cl-}$. The only positive ions present in the mixture are $\ce{H3O+}$.

First, the equilibrium mixture is filtered. Afterwards, the $[\ce{AuCl4-}]$ in the filtrate is determined. For this, an excess of potassium iodide solution is added to a 10.00 mL sample of the filtrate, which causes the following reactions:

$$\ce{AuCl4^-(aq) + 2 I^-(aq) -> AuCl2^-(aq) + I2(aq) + 2 Cl^-(aq)}$$

and

$$\ce{AuCl2^-(aq) + I^-(aq) -> AuI(s) + 2 Cl^-(aq)}$$

The iodine which is produced, is then titrated with a solution of sodium thiosulphate, which causes the following reaction:

$$\ce{2 S2O3^{2-}(aq) + I2(aq) -> S4O6^{2-}(aq) + 2 I^-(aq)}$$

This titration required 5.34 mL of a 0.0100 M sodium thiosulphate solution.

It can be assumed that the filtration, addition of potassium iodide solution, and the titration do not cause a shift of equilibrium I.

5 (3 points) Calculate the $[\ce{AuCl4-}]$ in $\mathrm{mol\,L^{-1}}$ of the investigated equilibrium mixture.

After the $[\ce{AuCl4-}]$ is known, more has to be determined in order to be able to calculate the equilibrium constant.

The $[\ce{AuCl2-}]$ in the equilibrium mixture can be calculated by filtering the mixture that was created after the titration and determining the mass of the residue. With this, and the amount of mmol of $\ce{AuCl4-}$ in the 10.00 mL sample, you can calculate how many mmol of $\ce{AuCl2-}$ were present in the 10.00 mL sample.

6 (2 points) Explain how you can calculate the amount of mmol of $\ce{AuCl2-}$ in the 10.00 mL sample, using the amount of mmol of $\ce{AuI}$ in the residue and the amount of mmol of $\ce{AuCl4-}$ in the 10.00 mL sample.

By determining the pH of the equilibrium mixture, the $[\ce{Cl-}]$ in the equilibrium mixture can be calculated. This is because the $[\ce{H3O+}]$, the $[\ce{AuCl4-}]$, the $[\ce{AuCl2-}]$ and the $[\ce{Cl-}]$ are related.

7 (2 points) What is the relation between the $[\ce{H3O+}]$, the $[\ce{AuCl4-}]$, the $[\ce{AuCl2-}]$ and the $[\ce{Cl-}]$ in the equilibrium mixture? Explain your answer.

8 (2 points) Does the concentration of $\ce{Au}$ still need to be determined in order to calculate the equilibrium constant of equilibrium I? Explain your answer.

problems.problem:
Problem 3 (16 points). Vasa

Epoxyalkanes are compounds that can be thought of as being derived from alkanes by replacing per molecule two H atoms on two different C atoms with one O atom. Examples of epoxyalkanes are:

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/nl-2024-1-11-fig1.png

Epoxyalkanes in which the oxygen atom in the molecules is bonded to two adjacent carbon atoms can easily polymerize under the influence of sodium hydroxide. This produces polyepoxyethane from epoxyethane. This polymer is often used to preserve wooden ships that have been under water for a very long time. This happened, among other things, with the Swedish warship Vasa, which capsized in the Stockholm harbor on its maiden voyage in 1628. From April 1961, when the ship resurfaced, it was treated with polyepoxyethane for 17 years.

A molecule of polyepoxyethane can be represented as follows:

$$\mathrm{H{-}(O{-}CH_2{-}CH_2)}_{n}\mathrm{{-}OH}$$

The value of $n$ in this formula can vary from less than 10 to more than 100. The formation of such a polymer molecule follows a mechanism with a number of successive steps.

The first step (initiation) is the attachment of a hydroxide ion to an epoxyethane molecule:

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/nl-2024-1-11-fig2.png

Then, starting from ion A, a number of successive propagation steps take place. A negative ion is formed again and again.

4 (3 points) Starting from ion A, show the first two successive propagation steps in structural formulas.

1,2-epoxypropane can also polymerize under the influence of sodium hydroxide. This polymerization proceeds by the same mechanism as the polymerization of epoxyethane.

5 (3 points) Show a part of the middle of a polymer molecule of poly-1,2-epoxypropane in structural formula. This part must be composed of three monomer units.

In polymerizations of epoxyalkanes, a series of successive propagation steps is terminated by a reaction with a water molecule (termination reaction). Research into the polymerization of epoxyethane under the influence of sodium hydroxide showed that, depending on the conditions under which the polymerization is carried out, different types of polyepoxyethane with different melting ranges can be obtained.

In one of the experiments in this study, an amount of polyepoxyethane with a mass of 92 grams was formed from 88 grams of epoxyethane. In this experiment there was no epoxyethane left at the end.

6 (3 points) Give the reaction equation for the mentioned termination reaction. Use the formula $\mathrm{H{-}(O{-}CH_2{-}CH_2)}_{n}\mathrm{{-}OH}$ for the end product.

7 (4 points) Calculate the average value of $n$ in the polyepoxyethane molecules $\mathrm{H{-}(O{-}CH_2{-}CH_2)}_{n}\mathrm{{-}OH}$ that are formed during the experiments described above.

Two other experiments from this study are described below.

$$\begin{array}{l|c|c|c} & & \text{fabric used} & \\ \hline & \text{epoxyethane (mol)} & \ce{NaOH}\ \text{(mol)} & \ce{H2O}\ \text{(mol)} \\ \hline \text{experiment 1} & 1.0 & 0.036 & 0.33 \\ \hline \text{experiment 2} & 1.0 & 0.036 & 0.10 \end{array}$$

Both experiments took place at the same temperature and pressure.
After polymerization of all epoxyethane, the polyepoxyethane was separated from the resulting reaction mixture. One of the experiments showed that polyepoxyethane was formed with a melting range of $+2\,^\circ\mathrm{C}$ to $+4\,^\circ\mathrm{C}$, while in the other experiment the melting range of the resulting polyepoxyethane was $+31\,^\circ\mathrm{C}$ to $+33\,^\circ\mathrm{C}$.

8 (3 points) Explain which of the two experiments produced polyepoxyethane with the highest melting range.

For sustainable energy, hydrogen seems to be a suitable energy carrier. In a fuel cell, hydrogen can be efficiently used for the production of electrical energy. $$\ce{BH4^{-}(aq) + 2 H2O(l) -> BO2^{-}(aq) + 4 H2(g)}$$

They ensure the complete conversion of $\ce{NaBH4}$ into $\ce{H2}$. Kinetic studies have shown that the catalytic hydrolysis of $\ce{NaBH4}$ is a zero-order reaction with respect to the concentration of $\ce{BH4-}$ and is directly proportional to the amount of Ru.

Problem 2 (24 points). A high-temperature superconductor

Superconductors are materials in which an electric current can flow without encountering resistance. Superconductivity was first discovered in 1911 by the Dutch (Leiden) scientist Heike Kamerlingh Onnes during his groundbreaking work in the field of extremely low temperatures. Superconductors are useful for various applications, such as in MRI, for example. However, a drawback is that most materials only become superconducting when cooled to near the absolute zero point. It was, therefore, a breakthrough when Georg Bednorz and Alex Müller discovered a class of ceramic materials that are already superconducting when cooled with liquid nitrogen. For this discovery of high-temperature superconductors, they were awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1987.

Among the best known examples of these ceramic superconductors are substances that can be represented by YBCO. These are composed of ions of yttrium (Y), barium, copper, and oxygen. The ions of yttrium (Y), barium, and copper occur in a ratio of 1 : 2 : 3. The number of oxide ions in the empirical formula of YBCO depends on the amount of oxygen that reacts during the preparation of a YBCO compound but is at most 7. The empirical formula of a YBCO compound can then be represented as $\mathrm{YBa_2Cu_3O_{(7-\mathit{x})}}$.

In the preparation of $\mathrm{YBa_2Cu_3O_{(7-\mathit{x})}}$, yttrium(III) carbonate, barium carbonate and copper(II) carbonate are allowed to react with each other in the presence of oxygen. Besides $\mathrm{YBa_2Cu_3O_{(7-\mathit{x})}}$, only carbon dioxide is formed.

To determine the value of $x$ in a YBCO compound, an iodometric titration can be performed. Initially, the YBCO compound is allowed to react with hydrochloric acid. This results in a solution in which no $\ce{Cu^{3+}}$ is present because it has reacted with water. This reaction of $\ce{Cu^{3+}}$ with water is a redox reaction that produces, among other things, $\ce{Cu^{2+}}$ and $\ce{O2}$.

Afterwards, an excess of potassium iodide is added to the solution, leading to the following reaction:

$$\ce{2 Cu^{2+} + 4 I- -> 2 CuI + I2}$$

Finally, the formed iodine is titrated with a solution of sodium thiosulfate, $\ce{Na2S2O3}$. The following reaction occurs in the titration:

$$\ce{2 S2O3^{2-} + I2 -> S4O6^{2-} + 2 I-}$$

In such a determination, 160 mg of YBCO compound was used. For the titration of the formed iodine, 21.8 mL of 0.0332 M sodium thiosulfate solution was required.

Penicillin is used as the collective term for the group of various types of penicillin. Penicillin has a bactericidal effect and is a commonly used antibiotic to combat infectious diseases.

Sir Alexander Fleming discovered penicillin (later called penicillin G) in 1928, as a product of the fungus Penicillium notatum. Fleming received the Nobel Prize in Medicine in 1945 for his discovery, along with Florey and Chain, who investigated the action of penicillin.
Due to the highly useful properties of penicillin, many years have been spent developing its syntheses. In this problem, a part of the synthesis of a certain type of penicillin developed by Professor J.C. Sheenan is considered.

$\mathbf{1}$ is reacted with acetic anhydride; in this reaction $\mathbf{2}$ (see below) is formed.
By increasing the temperature, $\mathbf{2}$ is converted into an intermediate product $\mathbf{3}$.

The bactericidal action of penicillin is based on the inhibition of bacterial cell wall formation. The cell wall of a bacterium consists, amongst other things, of a polysaccharide. Peptide chains, formed from a number of amino acids, are bound to this polysaccharide. The first amino acid bound to the polysaccharide is always alanine, with the amino group of alanine always linked to the polysaccharide. During the creation of the cell wall, two adjacent peptide chains are linked together. This linking is catalyzed by the enzyme transpeptidase. Two of such linkings are schematically shown below.

problems.problem:
Problem 4 (15 points). Methyl isocyanide

The compound methyl isocyanide can be converted to acetonitrile via an isomerization reaction according to:

$$\mathrm{CH_3NC\,(g)}\ \xrightarrow{\ k_\mathrm{exp}\ }\ \mathrm{CH_3CN\,(g)}$$

From experiments, it is evident that this reaction is a first-order reaction at high pressure and a second-order reaction at low pressure.

The mechanism of this isomerization reaction consists of two steps.

In a first step, a molecule of methyl isocyanide is activated to $\ce{CH3NC^{*}}$ by collision with another molecule of methyl isocyanide. With this activated molecule, the following can occur:
1. it is converted back to the original molecule of methyl isocyanide by collision with an inactivated molecule of methyl isocyanide;
2. it reacts in a second step to form a molecule of the isomer acetonitrile.

$$\mathrm{CH_3NC\,(g) + CH_3NC\,(g)}\ \underset{k_{-1}}{\overset{k_1}{\rightleftharpoons}}\ \mathrm{CH_3NC^{*}\,(g) + CH_3NC\,(g)}\qquad(1)$$

$$\mathrm{CH_3NC^{*}\,(g)}\ \xrightarrow{\ k_2\ }\ \mathrm{CH_3CN\,(g)}\qquad(2)$$

Using the ‘steady-state’ approximation, it can be derived that the rate equation for the formation of acetonitrile according to this mechanism is equal to:

$$\frac{d[\mathrm{CH_3CN}]}{dt} = \frac{k_1k_2[\mathrm{CH_3NC}]^2}{k_{-1}[\mathrm{CH_3NC}] + k_2}$$

14 (7 points) Give this derivation.

15 (2 points) Derive the expression for $k_\mathrm{exp}$ using the rate equation given above question 14.

With the help of the above rate equation, it can be derived that the conversion of methyl isocyanide to acetonitrile is a first-order reaction at high pressure and a second-order reaction at low pressure. This is because at high pressure $s_{-1} \gg s_2$, and at low pressure $s_{-1} \ll s_2$. Here, $s_{-1}$ represents the rate of the reaction to the left in equilibrium (1), and $s_2$ represents the rate of reaction (2).

16 (2 points) Explain that at high pressure $s_{-1} \gg s_2$ and at low pressure $s_{-1} \ll s_2$.

17 (4 points) Explain, based on the above data, that the conversion of methyl isocyanide to acetonitrile is a first-order reaction at high pressure and a second-order reaction at low pressure.

$$[\ce{N2O5}]_t = (V_\infty - V_t) \times F$$

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/nl-2025-3-3-fig2.png

10 (2 points) What type of reaction is this?

Until now, the para-aminophenol required for the production of paracetamol has mainly been obtained, through a series of steps, from benzene. The disadvantage of this route is that benzene is derived from crude oil. Recently, researchers have discovered a new synthesis method that uses a renewable raw material: lignin. Lignin is a complex organic compound which gives wood its strength. When lignin is reacted with dilute sodium hydroxide, a mixture of simple organic compounds is formed. From this mixture, the substance para-hydroxybenzoic acid ($\mathbf{I}$) can be isolated. The structural formula of para-hydroxybenzoic acid is depicted below:

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/nl-2025-3-3-fig3.png

Through three conversion steps, para-hydroxybenzoic acid ($\mathbf{I}$) can be transformed into para-aminophenol ($\mathbf{IV}$) via intermediate compounds $\mathbf{II}$ and $\mathbf{III}$:

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/nl-2025-3-3-fig4.png

11 (1 point) Give the structural formula of the substance that reacts with para-hydroxybenzoic acid in conversion step $\mathbf{1}$.

To form compound $\mathbf{III}$ from compound $\mathbf{II}$, an ammonia solution is used. Direct formation of $\mathbf{III}$ from $\mathbf{I}$ using an ammonia solution is not feasible, as an undesirable side reaction might occur.

12 (2 points) Which side reaction might take place?

In conversion step $\mathbf{3}$, a Hofmann rearrangement takes place. In this reaction, a C–C bond in the molecule is replaced by a C–N bond. The reaction proceeds with bromine in a basic medium. During the process, the following isocyanate is formed:

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/nl-2025-3-3-fig5.png

For the formation of the isocyanate, the following reaction mechanism is often proposed:

• an $\ce{OH-}$ ion binds a $\ce{H+}$ ion attached to the nitrogen atom;
• next, a $\ce{Br+}$ ion from a $\ce{Br2}$ molecule binds to the nitrogen atom, with formation of a $\ce{Br-}$ ion;
• then, a second $\ce{OH-}$ ion binds the other $\ce{H+}$ ion attached to the nitrogen atom; at the same time, a double bond forms between the N atom and the C atom, and a single bond forms between the C atom and the O atom;
• finally, a $\ce{Br-}$ ion is eliminated and the N atom becomes bonded to the benzene ring.

13 (6 points) Represent this mechanism using chemical equations with structural formulas.

• Draw all relevant lone pairs;
• use curly arrows ($\curvearrowright$) to indicate how electron pairs shift during bond formation and bond breaking;
• place all formal charges in the correct positions.

Through the addition of a water molecule to a molecule of the isocyanate, followed by the elimination of a molecule $\mathbf{X}$, a molecule of para-aminophenol is formed.

14 (3 points) Give the structural formula of the addition product of water and the isocyanate, and give the molecular formula of $\mathbf{X}$.

One disadvantage of this synthetic route to para-aminophenol is that the yield of the Hofmann rearrangement is rather low, resulting in an overall yield of less than 20%. This can be improved by replacing conversion step $\mathbf{1}$ with a reaction in which para-hydroxybenzoic acid is reacted with chloromethoxymethane,

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/nl-2025-3-3-fig6.png

(methoxymethyl chloride, commonly abbreviated as Mom-Cl).

This reaction protects both OH groups of the para-hydroxybenzoic acid molecule against side reactions.

The resulting product $\mathbf{V}$ can be represented as

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/nl-2025-3-3-fig7.png

The reaction between chloromethoxymethane and para-hydroxybenzoic acid begins with the elimination of a chloride ion from a molecule of chloromethoxymethane. The resulting positively charged ion is ‘stabilised by resonance’.

15 (4 points) Draw the resonance structures of the positive ion.

16 (1 point) Give the full structural formula of compound $\mathbf{V}$.

The entire synthetic route using chloromethoxymethane is depicted below:

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/nl-2025-3-3-fig8.png

The percentage yield of each conversion step is indicated in the figure.

Poplar wood is often used as a source of lignin. If you want to know how much poplar wood is required to synthesise a given number of kilograms of paracetamol, you must multiply that amount of kg of paracetamol by a factor $F$:

$$\text{amount of poplar wood (kg)} = \text{amount of paracetamol (kg)} \times F.$$

17 (6 points) Calculate the value of $F$. In addition to the given conversion percentages, use the following data:

problems.title: Tankyrase inhibitors
problems.problem:
Problem 4 (8 points). Tankyrase inhibitors

Tankyrase is an enzyme capable of attaching small chemical tags, known as ADP-ribose chains, to proteins. These tags may serve as signals indicating that a protein should be broken down, or they may alter the way a protein functions. Overexpression of tankyrase, that is the production of excessive amounts of this enzyme, has been linked to the development of cancer, as it disrupts the normal regulation of cell growth. Inhibiting tankyrase is therefore considered a promising strategy for the treatment of such conditions. Researchers at Symeres are actively engaged in the development of compounds that can act as tankyrase inhibitors.

Shown below are the structures of two compounds ($\mathbf{I}$ and $\mathbf{II}$) that have been synthesised and investigated for their ability to inhibit tankyrase activity.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/nl-2025-3-4-fig1.png

Due to the presence of the Cl atoms, rotation around the relevant C–N bonds is hindered at room temperature. As a result, $\mathbf{I}$ and $\mathbf{II}$ are stereoisomers

18 (2 points) Explain whether $\mathbf{I}$ and $\mathbf{II}$ are enantiomers or diastereomers.

Aside from $\mathbf{II}$, two other stereoisomers of $\mathbf{I}$ exist.

19 (3 points) Explain why, aside from $\mathbf{II}$, two other stereoisomers of $\mathbf{I}$ exist.

At elevated temperatures, the stereoisomers $\mathbf{I}$ and $\mathbf{II}$ gradually convert into one another due to the fact that rotation around the relevant C–N bonds becomes possible. This isomerisation follows first-order kinetics. Starting from compound $\mathbf{I}$, after 72 hours at a temperature of 70 °C, 10 percent has been converted into compound $\mathbf{II}$.

20 (3 points) Calculate how many hours it will take to convert 1.0 percent of compound $\mathbf{I}$ to compound $\mathbf{II}$, at 70 °C. Assume that the reverse conversion from $\mathbf{II}$ to $\mathbf{I}$ is negligible.

Problem 5 (11 points). Shono oxidation

The synthesis of compounds by means of electrolysis is referred to as electrosynthesis. At Symeres, a research group specialises in the use of electrosynthesis to introduce functional groups into simple molecules, with the aim of using the introduced groups as ‘scaffolds’ for the construction of complex molecules.

An example of this type of electrosynthesis, a so-called Shono oxidation, is schematically represented below:

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/nl-2025-3-5-fig1.png

$\mathbf{I}$ is a model molecule in which the nitrogen atom of a morpholine ring is bound to a protecting group (–COR). During the electrolysis, a highly selective methoxylation of the morpholine ring takes place.

21 (2 points) Explain whether the conversion of compound $\mathbf{I}$ to the intermediate takes place at the positive electrode or at the negative electrode.

22 (2 points) Verify, on the basis of the diagram, whether the methoxylation is regioselective.

23 (2 points) Verify, on the basis of the diagram, whether the methoxylation is stereoselective.

The following is a representative example of the way in which this Shono oxidation can be carried out:

0.41 mol of compound $\mathbf{I}$ is dissolved in 400 mL of methanol. An inert electrolyte is added. The solution is electrolysed using graphite electrodes. The electrolysis lasts for 15 hours, during which a current of 1.7 A is maintained.

The yield of the conversion of compound $\mathbf{I}$ to compound $\mathbf{II}$ is 92 percent.

The efficiency of the current usage (the percentage of the electric current used for the formation of the product) in this Shono oxidation is high.

problems.title: Cobalt Complexes
problems.problem:
Problem 6 (22 points). Cobalt Complexes

Cobalt is a transition metal. In nature, it is primarily found in compounds containing $\ce{Co^{2+}}$ ions. Cobalt ions with a 3+ charge can also exist, but do not occur naturally, as $\ce{Co^{3+}}$ is a very strong oxidising agent.

Both cobalt ions, $\ce{Co^{2+}}$ and $\ce{Co^{3+}}$, can form stable complexes with ammonia molecules.

Below is an overview of half-reactions of various forms of cobalt. The standard electrode potential is included for several of them.

$$\begin{array}{ll} \ce{Co^{3+} + 3 e- -> Co} & E^0 = +0.46\,\mathrm{V} \\ \ce{Co^{3+} + e- -> Co^{2+}} & \\ \ce{Co^{2+} + 2 e- -> Co} & E^0 = -0.29\,\mathrm{V} \\ \ce{Co(NH3)6^{3+} + 3 e- -> Co + 6 NH3} & \\ \ce{Co(NH3)6^{3+} + e- -> Co(NH3)6^{2+}} & E^0 = +0.1\,\mathrm{V} \\ \ce{Co(NH3)6^{2+} + 2 e- -> Co + 6 NH3} & E^0 = -0.42\,\mathrm{V} \end{array}$$

To find the change in Gibbs free energy in a redox (half) reaction, the following formula can be applied: $\Delta G = -n \times F \times \Delta E$.

25 (4 points) Calculate, based on data from the overview above, the value of the standard electrode potential for the half-reaction $\ce{Co^{3+} + e- -> Co^{2+}}$.

The stability of the $\ce{Co(NH3)6^{3+}}$ complex is related to the following equilibrium:

$$\ce{Co^{3+} + 6 NH3 <=> Co(NH3)6^{3+}} \qquad \text{equilibrium 1 with } K = 1.0\cdot10^{33}$$

26 (4 points) Calculate, based on data provided in this question, the value of the standard electrode potential for the half-reaction $\ce{Co(NH3)6^{3+} + 3 e- -> Co + 6 NH3}$.

Complex cobalt ions give a characteristic colour to solutions. For example, a solution of the salt complex $\ce{Co(NH3)6Cl3}$ exhibits a dark purple colour. The graph below shows the UV–VIS spectrum of a $1.00\cdot10^{-3}$ M solution of $\ce{Co(NH3)6Cl3}$.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/nl-2025-3-6-fig1.png

A cuvette with an optical path length of 1.00 cm was used when recording the spectrum.

27 (3 points) Calculate, based on this UV–VIS spectrum, the molar extinction coefficient, $\varepsilon$, of $\ce{Co(NH3)6^{3+}}$ at 475 nm. Assume that only $\ce{Co(NH3)6^{3+}}$ absorbs light in the solution.

The compound $\ce{Co(NH3)6Cl3}$ is formed in four steps:

$$\begin{array}{l} \ce{CoCl2.6H2O + NH4Cl -> Co(H2O)6^{2+} + NH4+ + 3 Cl-} \\ \ce{Co(H2O)6^{2+} + 6 NH3 -> Co(NH3)6^{2+} + 6 H2O} \\ \ce{Co(NH3)6^{2+} + 1/2 H2O2 -> Co(NH3)6^{3+} + OH-} \\ \ce{Co(NH3)6^{3+} + 3 Cl- -> Co(NH3)6Cl3} \end{array}$$

The starting point is red cobalt(II) chloride hexahydrate. This is dissolved in boiling water, and ammonium chloride is added, resulting in the formation of the blue complex $\ce{Co(H2O)6^{2+}}$. Concentrated ammonia is then added, producing brown $\ce{Co(NH3)6^{2+}}$. Subsequently, this complex is oxidised with hydrogen peroxide to the dark purple complex $\ce{Co(NH3)6^{3+}}$, which then precipitates with chloride as $\ce{Co(NH3)6Cl3}$.

During an experiment, $\ce{Co(NH3)6Cl3}$ is synthesised via the above reactions, starting with 6.0065 g of cobalt(II) chloride hexahydrate. Ultimately, 5.4543 g of impure product is obtained. From this impure product, 30.0 mg is dissolved in a 100.0 mL volumetric flask. The absorbance of this solution is measured at 475 nm and found to be 0.122. The optical path length of the cuvette used was 1.00 cm.

28 (8 points) Calculate the yield of this synthesis. Assume that the impurities do not absorb light at 475 nm.

Complexes of $\ce{Co^{3+}}$ with ammonia also exist in which one or more ammonia molecules are replaced by one or more chloride ions. The general formula of these complexes can be represented as $[\mathrm{Co(NH_3)}_{6-x}\mathrm{Cl}_x]^{n+}$, where $x$ is an integer.

29 (1 point) What is the relationship between $n$ and $x$?

Below are the spatial structures of three of these complexes, for which $x$ equals 1, 2, and 3, respectively.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/nl-2025-3-6-fig2.png

An isomer exists for complex II and complex III.

The worksheet accompanying this test, contains outlines for the isomers of the complexes II and III.

[The outlines printed on the worksheet:]

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/nl-2025-3-6-fig3.png

30 (2 points) Draw the isomer of complex II and the isomer of complex III on your worksheet.

$$\begin{array}{l|c|c} \text{Acid name} & \text{Molar concentration in the pilsner } (\mathrm{mmol\,L^{-1}}) & \text{Number of COOH groups per molecule} \\ \hline \text{malic acid} & 0.433 & 2 \\ \text{pyruvic acid} & 0.545 & 1 \\ \text{lactic acid} & 1.099 & 1 \\ \text{acetic acid} & 0.466 & 1 \\ \text{citric acid} & 0.562 & 3 \\ \text{succinic acid} & 0.415 & 2 \\ \text{fumaric acid} & 0.362 & 2 \\ \hline \textit{total} & \mathit{3.882} & \end{array}$$

2. (2 points) Show this calculation.

The analysed pilsner contains, in addition to the COOH groups from the acids listed in Table 1, COOH groups from other organic acids as well. These COOH groups are referred to below as the extra COOH groups.

Step 1: A bonding pair of electrons between the O atom and the N atom in intermediate $\mathbf{3}$ binds an H atom from the adjacent N atom. A double bond between the N atoms is created through bond rearrangement.
Step 2: A proton is transferred from the N atom to a water molecule.
Step 3: One of the non-bonding electron pairs on the O atom of the OH group created in step 1 binds a proton from an $\ce{H3O+}$ ion.
Step 4: By displacement of bonding and non-bonding electron pairs, $\ce{H2O}$ leaves the molecule and ion $\mathbf{2}$ is formed.

10. (8 points) Represent steps 1 to 4 of the mechanism using structural formulas. Use the information below.
• Use the notation $\mathbf{R}$ for the side group:

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/nl-2026-2-11-fig4.png

• Draw all bonding and non-bonding electron pairs.
• Indicate with curly arrows ($\curvearrowright$) how electron pairs move.
• Place all formal charges in the correct place.

In a second reaction, a diazonium coupling occurs between ion $\mathbf{2}$ and N,N-dimethylaniline according to the incomplete reaction equation below.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/nl-2026-2-11-fig5.png

In this incomplete reaction equation, one particle is missing.

11. (1 point) Give the formula for the missing particle in the incomplete reaction equation above and indicate whether it should be placed before or after the arrow.

This reaction can occur because N,N-dimethylaniline has resonance structures where positions with a 1– charge exist in the benzene ring. This delocalization also involves the N atom. One of these resonance structures results in the formation of a methyl red molecule.

12. (2 points) Draw this resonance structure. Give your answer as Lewis structure including all formal charges in the correct place.

Methyl red is a weak acid. When methyl red is added to a colourless solution, the resulting colour depends on the pH of the solution. The following equilibrium plays a role:

$$\ce{mrH + H2O <=> H3O+ + mr-}$$

where $\ce{mr-}$ is the conjugate base of methyl red (mrH). The $\mathrm{p}K_\mathrm{a}$ of methyl red is 5.00.

At high pH, $\ce{mr-}$ absorbs maximum light at a wavelength of $429\ \mathrm{nm}$, and at low pH, mrH absorbs maximum light at a wavelength of $520\ \mathrm{nm}$. By measuring the absorbance at $429\ \mathrm{nm}$ ($A_{429}$) and at $520\ \mathrm{nm}$ ($A_{520}$), the concentrations of mrH and $\ce{mr-}$ can be determined using the Lambert-Beer law. From this, the pH of the solution can then be calculated.

The table below gives the molar extinction coefficients of mrH and $\ce{mr-}$ at two wavelengths.

problems.title: Trouble in a cylinder

Problem 1 (10 points). Trouble in a cylinder

A cylinder sealed by a movable piston contains a quantity of propane. The cylinder is heated to $527\ ^\circ\mathrm{C}$. The following equilibrium is established:

$$\ce{C3H8(g) <=> C3H6(g) + H2(g)}\qquad\text{with } K_\mathrm{c} = 1{,}30\cdot10^{-3}$$

When equilibrium has been reached, the volume percentage of propane is equal to 80%.

1. (7 points) Calculate $[\ce{C3H8}]$, $[\ce{C3H6}]$, $[\ce{H2}]$, all in $\mathrm{mol\,dm^{-3}}$, and the total pressure, in Pa, in the cylinder when equilibrium has been reached.

Next, the piston is pushed in until the volume is reduced by half while maintaining a constant temperature.

problems.title: Malaprade
problems.problem:
Problem 2 (19 points). Malaprade

Organic compounds with certain functional groups in the molecule that are bonded to neighboring (vicinal) carbon atoms can react with sodium periodate ($\ce{NaIO4}$). In this reaction, the bond between the carbon atoms to which the functional groups are attached is broken, while the groups bound to those carbon atoms are also transformed. The following rules apply:
• When the functional group is a hydroxyl group, it is converted into a carbonyl group.
• When the functional group is a carbonyl group, it is converted into a carboxyl group.
• When the functional group is a carboxyl group, it is converted into carbon dioxide.

This reaction may be referred to as the Malaprade reaction. The Malaprade reaction is a redox reaction.

For example: 2-hydroxy-2-methylpropanal is converted by periodate into methanoic acid and propanone in a molar ratio 1 : 1; the periodate is converted into iodate ($\ce{IO3-}$):

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/nl-2026-3-2-fig1.png

3. (2 points) Give the structural formula of the compound that yields ethanoic acid as the sole product in the Malaprade reaction.

The Malaprade reaction can be used, among others, to determine the concentration of glycol (ethane-1,2-diol) in solution. A glycol solution is commonly used as antifreeze.

In such a determination, $150\ \mathrm{mg}$ of antifreeze was added to a $25.0\ \mathrm{mL}$ solution of sodium periodate (in excess). The following reaction occurred:

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/nl-2026-3-2-fig2.png

After the reaction was complete, the solution was acidified and an excess amount of iodide was added. Both the $\ce{IO4-}$ and the formed $\ce{IO3-}$ reacted with iodide to form $\ce{I2}$:

$$\ce{IO4- + 7 I- + 8 H+ -> 4 I2 + 4 H2O}$$

and

$$\ce{IO3- + 5 I- + 6 H+ -> 3 I2 + 3 H2O}$$

Finally, the formed iodine was titrated with a $0.502\ \mathrm{M}$ solution of sodium thiosulfate. The following reaction occurred:

$$\ce{I2 + 2 S2O3^{2-} -> 2 I- + S4O6^{2-}}$$

The titration required $19.6\ \mathrm{mL}$ of the sodium thiosulfate solution.

Next, a blank determination was performed, as described above, but without adding the antifreeze. For this blank determination, $23.9\ \mathrm{mL}$ of the sodium thiosulfate solution was required to titrate the formed iodine.

4. (8 points) Calculate the mass percentage of glycol in the antifreeze sample.

The Malaprade reaction can also be used to distinguish between certain sugars. For example the Malaprade reaction can be used to determine whether a sugar is glucose or fructose.

During the Malaprade reaction with glucose and fructose, all C – C bonds in the molecules are broken. The following substances can then be formed: methanal, methanoic acid and carbon dioxide.

5. (9 points) Answer the following questions:
• Which substances are finally formed in the Malaprade reaction of glucose, and in what molar ratio are these substances formed?
• Which substances are finally formed in the Malaprade reaction of fructose, and in what molar ratio are these substances formed?
• How could you determine whether a sugar is glucose or fructose: by determining the molar ratio in which glucose and fructose react with periodate, or by titrating the reaction products of the Malaprade reaction with sodium hydroxide? Explain your answer.

Use the information provided at the beginning of this problem and the open-chain structures of glucose and fructose:

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/nl-2026-3-2-fig3.png

problems.title: Electrochemical conversion of CO2
problems.problem:
Problem 3 (23 points). Electrochemical conversion of $\ce{CO2}$

The electrochemical conversion of $\ce{CO2}$ is seen as a promising and technically feasible method for mitigating the negative effects of rising $\ce{CO2}$ levels in the atmosphere.
Using renewable energy, $\ce{CO2}$ can be converted into various platform chemicals.
To ensure that the formation of desired products during electrolysis proceeds at a practically feasible rate, research is conducted into the use of electrocatalysts.
A new concept in the field of such catalysts is based on the use of electrodes coated in a foam-like material.
This foam-like material has a large surface area that is readily accessible to reactants (e.g $\ce{H2O}$, $\ce{H2}$ en $\ce{CO2}$).
Copper-based materials are the only known metallic electrocatalysts capable of producing hydrocarbons and alcohols in significant quantities through the electrolysis of $\ce{CO2}$.
During a specific electrolysis in an acidic medium, $\ce{CO2}$ is converted at the negative electrode into ethanol and propan-1-ol. In these conversions, 6 moles of electrons react per mole of converted $\ce{CO2}$.

6. (3 points) Provide the equation of the half-reaction for the conversion of $\ce{CO2}$ to propan-1-ol in an acidic medium.

The standard electrode potential for the conversion of $\ce{CO2}$ to ethanol can be calculated by considering a galvanic cell consisting of a standard $\ce{CO2}$/ethanol half-cell and a standard $\ce{H2}$/$\ce{H+}$ half-cell.
The reaction occurring in this galvanic cell can be represented by the following reaction equation:

$$\ce{2 CO2(g) + 6 H2(g) -> C2H6O(l) + 3 H2O(l)}$$

7. (5 points) Calculate the standard electrode potential for the conversion of $\ce{CO2}$ to ethanol. Use data from the information booklet and the formula $\Delta_\mathrm{r}G = -\,n\times F\times\Delta E$.

A representative example of the formation of electrode material with a copper-based metallic foam layer is described below:
Electrolysis is carried out in an acidic solution containing both copper(II) ions and silver ions. A copper plate with a surface area of $1.0\ \mathrm{cm^2}$ serves as the negative electrode, while platinum foil acts as the positive electrode. During electrolysis, a layer of porous, foam-like Cu-Ag bimetal deposits on the negative electrode. This porous structure of the bimetal forms because tiny hydrogen bubbles evolve within the bimetal during the metal deposition. The bimetal is, so to speak, slightly inflated.
A layer of foam containing $5.4\ \mathrm{mg}$ of Cu-Ag bimetal forms on the copper plate.
This bimetal contains 90% Cu by mass and 10% Ag.
During this electrolysis $60\ \mathrm{C\,cm^{-2}}$ of charge was used.

8. (4 points) Calculate the Faraday efficiency (FE in %) of this metal deposition.
FE is defined as $\dfrac{Q_\text{product}}{Q_\text{total}}\times100\%$. $Q$ represents the amount of electric charge.

The Cu-Ag bimetallic foam catalyst (90 wt% Cu; 10 wt% Ag) is used in a $\ce{CO2}$ electrolysis experiment:
$35\ \mathrm{mL}$ of $0.5\ \mathrm{M}$ $\ce{KHCO3}$ electrolyte solution saturated with $\ce{CO2}$ is electrolyzed.
The negative copper electrode is coated with the Cu-Ag bimetallic foam catalyst and the positive electrode is made of platinum. The $\ce{CO2}$ electrolysis is carried out at a constant current density of $J = 30\ \mathrm{mA\,cm^{-2}}$ for 1.0 hour (Note: the current density is normalized to a surface area of $1.0\ \mathrm{cm^2}$).
An analysis of the product after the electrolysis yields mass concentrations of $41.3\ \mathrm{mg\,L^{-1}}$ ethanol and $7.4\ \mathrm{mg\,L^{-1}}$ propan-1-ol. Both alcohols are liquid reaction products and accumulate in the electrolyte during the electrolysis. It may be assumed that only hydrogen gas ($\ce{H2}$) is formed as a byproduct at the negative electrode.

9. (2 points) Provide the equation for the half-reaction that occurs at the positive electrode.

In the electrolysis described above, 33.6 percent of the current is used for the production of ethanol and 6.9 percent for the production of propan-1-ol.

10. (5 points) Calculate how many $\mathrm{cm^3}$ $\ce{H2}$ (at $p_0$ and $298\ \mathrm{K}$) is formed at the negative electrode.

11. (4 points) Calculate how many mg of $\ce{CO2}$ are converted in the electrolysis described above.
Assume that the total volume of the electrolyte, ethanol, and propan-1-ol remains $35\ \mathrm{mL}$.

problems.title: Crotonic acid
problems.problem:
Problem 4 (17 points). Crotonic acid

Crotonic acid has the following chemical structure:

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/nl-2026-3-4-fig1.png

12. (2 points) Copy this structural formula onto your answer sheet and write the type of hybridization for each carbon atom.

There are various synthetic routes for the production of crotonic acid. The byproducts often include the stereoisomer and a specific structural isomer $\mathbf{A}$ of crotonic acid. The mass spectra of crotonic acid and of this structural isomer $\mathbf{A}$ are shown below.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/nl-2026-3-4-fig2.png

13. (3 points) Perform the following tasks:
• Explain, based on these mass spectra, that $\mathbf{A}$ is a structural isomer of crotonic acid.
• Explain that it can be deduced from these mass spectra that $\mathbf{A}$, like crotonic acid, is also a carboxylic acid.

Crotonic acid can be obtained by the thermolysis of the biopolymer poly(3-hydroxybutanoic acid). This polymer can be produced by certain bacteria.

14. (3 points) Provide the structural formula of a fragment from the middle of a molecule of this polymer. This fragment must consist of three monomer units.

15. (2 points) Provide the reaction equation in molecular formulas for the thermolysis of poly(3-hydroxybutanoic acid) to crotonic acid.

Crotonic acid is used as a starting material in organic synthesis.
A specific synthetic route starts with the electrophilic addition of bromine to crotonic acid. This reaction yields 2,3-dibromobutanoic acid.
This addition reaction proceeds via a so-called anti-mechanism:
A bromine molecule reacts with a crotonic acid molecule. This produces a so-called bromonium ion and a bromide ion. In the bromonium ion, Br is located at the bottom or at the top of the ion. The bromide ion then reacts from the opposite side (anti), forming the product. This can result in the following product:

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/nl-2026-3-4-fig3.png

16. (3 points) Explain whether carbon atom 2 has the $R$ or the $S$ configuration. Include a drawing in your explanation.

In the structural formula shown for 2,3-dibromobutanoic acid, various stereoisomers are possible. However, not all of these are formed during the electrophilic addition of bromine to crotonic acid.

17. (2 points) Explain how many stereoisomers of 2,3-dibromobutanoic acid are possible in total, in principle.

18. (2 points) Explain how many stereoisomers of 2,3-dibromobutanoic acid are formed during the electrophilic addition of bromine to crotonic acid.

problems.title: CoFe
problems.problem:
Problem 5 (17 points). CoFe

The structure of the chloropentaamminecobalt(III) complex, $\ce{Co(Cl)(NH3)5^{2+}}$, is shown below.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/nl-2026-3-5-fig1.png

These complexes occur in a solution of chloropentaamminecobalt(III) chloride. An excess of a silver nitrate solution is added to $10.00\ \mathrm{mL}$ of a $0.0500\ \mathrm{M}$ solution of chloropentaamminecobalt(III) chloride. This produces a precipitate.

19. (3 points) Calculate how many g of precipitate are formed.

$\ce{Co(Cl)3(NH3)3}$ complexes also exist. Four structures with this formula are shown below:

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/nl-2026-3-5-fig2.png

20. (2 points) Which of these structures are identical?

A solution that contains complex ions $\ce{Co(Cl)(NH3)5^{2+}}$ is red in colour. The transmittance, $T$, of a solution with $[\ce{Co(Cl)(NH3)5^{2+}}] = 0.0200\ \mathrm{mol\,L^{-1}}$ is measured at $520\ \mathrm{nm}$ in a cuvette with a path length of $1.00\ \mathrm{cm}$. The transmittance is 7.50%.

21. (3 points) Calculate the molar extinction coefficient $\varepsilon$ of $\ce{Co(Cl)(NH3)5^{2+}}$. Assume that in this solution, only $\ce{Co(Cl)(NH3)5^{2+}}$ absorbs light.

When an acidified solution of iron(II) chloride is added to a solution containing $\ce{Co(Cl)(NH3)5^{2+}}$, the following reaction takes place:

$$\ce{Co(Cl)(NH3)5^{2+} + Fe^{2+} + 5 H+ -> Co^{2+} + FeCl^{2+} + 5 NH4+}$$

The speed of this reaction is given by $r = k[\ce{Co(Cl)(NH3)5^{2+}}][\ce{Fe^{2+}}]$.

To determine the rate constant $k$ of this reaction, an experiment is carried out in which $10.00\ \mathrm{mL}$ of a $0.300\ \mathrm{M}$ solution of iron(II) chloride is added to $10.00\ \mathrm{mL}$ of a solution containing $\ce{Co(Cl)(NH3)5^{2+}}$. Care is taken to ensure that the initial concentration of $\ce{Fe^{2+}}$ is many times greater than the concentration of $\ce{Co(Cl)(NH3)5^{2+}}$.

During the reaction, the absorbance $A$ of the solution is measured at $520\ \mathrm{nm}$ at various points in time. The following observations are obtained:

$$\begin{array}{c|c|c|c|c|c} t\ (\mathrm{min}) & 10 & 20 & 40 & 60 & \infty \\ \hline A & 1.15 & 0.875 & 0.558 & 0.410 & 0.283 \end{array}$$

The absorbance at $t = \infty$ is the absorbance measured once the reaction has finished.
For the calculation of $k$, you can assume that $[\ce{Co(Cl)(NH3)5^{2+}}]_t$ is proportional to $(E_t - E_\infty)$.

22. (1 point) Give a possible explanation for the fact that $E_\infty$ does not equal zero.

23. (2 points) Explain why $[\ce{Co(Cl)(NH3)5^{2+}}]_t$ is proportional to $(E_t - E_\infty)$.

24. (6 points) Calculate $k$ in the correct SI unit.

problems.title: Dipeptide
problems.problem:
Problem 6 (14 points). Dipeptide

Dipeptides are an important source of nitrogen and free amino acids within the cell. It turns out that transport of dipeptides across the cell membrane via specialised transport proteins is faster and, moreover, more energy-efficient than the transport of free amino acids. As a result, the cell efficiently takes in twice the amount of building blocks.

The dipeptide Ser – Ser dissolves easily in water; the structural formula for Ser – Ser can be represented as follows:

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/nl-2026-3-6-fig1.png

In a neutral solution, Ser – Ser is rarely found in the form shown in the structural formula above.

25. (1 point) Show, using a structural formula, how the dipeptide Ser – Ser mainly exists in a solution with a pH of 7.0.

A Ser – Ser molecule contains what is known as an amide group. The bond between the carbon atom and the nitrogen atom in this group behaves partly like a double bond.

26. (3 points) Explain this using electron configurations (resonance structures) of the amide group.

This also means that the bonds around the nitrogen atom lie in one plane and that Ser – Ser has $E$/$Z$ isomers. It turns out that one of the $E$/$Z$ isomers of Ser – Ser occurs much more frequently than the other one.

27. (3 points) Carry out the following tasks:
• Explain that Ser – Ser has $E$/$Z$ isomers.
• Draw a three-dimensional structure of the $E$/$Z$ isomer of Ser – Ser that occurs most frequently and explain why it occurs most frequently.

The formation of the dipeptide Ser – Ser is an equilibrium reaction:

$$\text{2 Ser} \rightleftharpoons \text{Ser – Ser} + \ce{H2O}\qquad\text{equilibrium 1}$$

For equilibrium 1, $\Delta G_1^0 = +1.7\cdot10^{4}\ \mathrm{J\,mol^{-1}}$.

In biological systems, the formation of dipeptides is linked to the hydrolysis of adenosine triphosphate (ATP), which produces adenosine diphosphate (ADP) and a phosphate group ($\mathrm{P_i}$):

$$\text{ATP} + \ce{H2O} \rightleftharpoons \text{ADP} + \mathrm{P_i}\qquad\text{equilibrium 2}$$

Possible formulas for $\mathrm{P_i}$ are $\ce{H3PO4}$, $\ce{H2PO4-}$, $\ce{HPO4^{2-}}$ and $\ce{PO4^{3-}}$.

28. (2 points) Which two of the options for $\mathrm{P_i}$ mentioned above are most common in a solution with a pH of 7.0?

For equilibrium 2, $\Delta G_2^0 = -\,2.8\cdot10^{4}\ \mathrm{J\,mol^{-1}}$.

Coupling equilibrium 2 with equilibrium 1 creates a new equilibrium:

$$\text{2 Ser} + \text{ATP} \rightleftharpoons \text{Ser – Ser} + \text{ADP} + \mathrm{P_i}\qquad\text{equilibrium 3}$$

29. (5 points) Carry out the following tasks:
• Calculate the equilibrium constant $K_{\mathrm{c},1}$ for equilibrium 1.
• Calculate the equilibrium constant $K_{\mathrm{c},3}$ for equilibrium 3.
• Explain how the coupling of the two equilibria affects the yield of the dipeptide.

problems.title: Hydrogen Storage
problems.problem:
Problem 7 (20 points). Hydrogen Storage

The alloy with the formula $\ce{LaNi5}$ is very suitable for the storage and transport of hydrogen.

The alloy can be prepared by allowing lanthanum(III) oxide and nickel(II) oxide to react in the correct ratio in the presence of an excess of calcium hydride. This also produces calcium hydroxide. Approximately twice as much calcium hydride is used as is theoretically required.

30. (3 points) Calculate the mass ratio in which lanthanum(III) oxide and nickel(II) oxide must react.
Write your answer as lanthanum(III) oxide : nickel(II) oxide = … : 1.0.

31. (4 points) Calculate how many grams of calcium hydride are used to synthesise $1.0\ \mathrm{g}$ of $\ce{LaNi5}$ if a twofold excess of calcium hydride is applied.

Once the reaction is complete, a mixture of the solids $\ce{LaNi5}$, calcium hydroxide and calcium hydride is obtained. The calcium hydroxide and calcium hydride have to be removed from this mixture.

32. (2 points) Explain how you could do this.

The unit cell of $\ce{LaNi5}$ has the following shape:

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/nl-2026-3-7-fig1.png

Here, the angles $\alpha$ and $\beta$ equal $90^\circ$ and the angle $\gamma$ equals $120^\circ$, whilst the edges are given by $a = b = 511\ \mathrm{pm}$ and $c = 397\ \mathrm{pm}$.

The formula of the unit cell is $\ce{LaNi5}$. The lanthanum atoms (the black dots) are located at the corners. In the full drawing of the unit cell of $\ce{LaNi5}$, 9 nickel atoms still have to be drawn.

33. (3 points) Explain where the nickel atoms can be located within the unit cell.

34. (3 points) Calculate the density of $\ce{LaNi5}$ in $\mathrm{kg\,m^{-3}}$. For this calculation, you will need the volume of the unit cell; if you are unable to calculate this, assume $V_\mathrm{cel} = 1.2\cdot10^{-28}\ \mathrm{m^3}$; this is not the correct volume.

Hydrogen atoms can occupy the spaces between the atoms in the $\ce{LaNi5}$ lattice. When all these spaces are filled with hydrogen atoms, the $\ce{LaNi5}$ alloy can hold $1\,244$ times as many hydrogen atoms per $\mathrm{cm^3}$ as are present in one $\mathrm{cm^3}$ of gaseous hydrogen at $273\ \mathrm{K}$ and $p = p_0$.

35. (5 points) Calculate the maximum number of hydrogen atoms that can be stored in one unit cell. For this calculation, you will need the volume of the unit cell; if you are unable to calculate this, assume $V_\mathrm{cel} = 1.2\cdot10^{-28}\ \mathrm{m^3}$; this is not the correct volume.
